**In-Person Testing Requirements for Texas Tech K-12**

**STAAR and EOC Exams:**
- **Yes, there are in-person testing requirements for full-time Texas Tech K-12 students.**
- All students in grades 3–8 and high school students enrolled in courses with End-of-Course (EOC) exams (Algebra I, Biology, English I, English II, U.S. History) **must take the State of Texas Assessments of Academic Readiness (STAAR) and EOC exams in person** at an approved testing site.

**For Students Living Outside Texas (Including International):**
- If you are outside Texas (such as in Venezuela), you must arrange for an approved proctor and testing location.
- The family is responsible for finding a local proctor (such as a school official or librarian) and submitting their information to Texas Tech K-12 for approval before testing.
- The Texas Tech K-12 testing department will provide guidance and must approve the proctor and site before the exam.

**Online Courses and Credit by Exams (CBEs):**
- Most course final exams and CBEs use online proctoring (Proctorio), which can be completed remotely and do not require in-person attendance.

**Summary:**
- **STAAR/EOC:** In-person, proctored testing is required.
- **Course finals/CBEs:** Generally completed online with remote proctoring.

**1. Application & Program Selection**
- Complete the Texas Tech K-12 Intake Form online: [Texas Tech K-12 Intake Form](https://ttu.focusschoolsoftware.com/focus/apply/?_gl=1*v05loa*_gcl_au*NTY5NzA2ODU2LjE3MzA4NDA5OTY.*_ga*MjU0NDE2Nzg2LjE3MjMwNDQ2MTA.*_ga_TSPQSJQPQF*MTczMzI2MjA5Ni4xNzkuMS4xNzMzMjYyMTA1LjAuMC4w)
- On page 2, select the most appropriate program for your student:
  - Full-time Tuition-Free Diploma Program (TX residents only, lottery-based)
  - Full-time Tuition-Paid Diploma Program (for non-TX residents or those seeking more flexibility)

**2. Required Documentation**
- Submit the following:
  - Birth certificate
  - Proof of Texas residency (for tuition-free program)
  - Unofficial transcript
  - For homeschool students: provide a transcript and be prepared to take Credit By Exams (CBEs) for grade placement

**3. Lottery & Enrollment Dates (Tuition-Free Program)**
- Mid-year (Spring) lottery for tuition-free program is held October 29, 2026.
- For new students, course enrollments open January 4, 2027. Courses must be completed by June 30, 2027.
- If not selected in the lottery, you’ll be placed on a waitlist and notified if a spot opens.

**4. Tuition-Paid Program**
- Enrollment is available year-round; students can begin courses at any time.
- Payment is due upon enrollment. No payment plans are offered.

**5. Course Load & Progress**
- Seniors must be enrolled in at least four semester courses and maintain satisfactory progress.
- All courses must be completed within the designated semester timeline (no extensions).
- Attendance is tracked by progress: complete at least 5% of each course's assignments each week.

**6. State Testing Requirements**
- Participation in mandatory state testing (STAAR/EOC) is required for graduation and continued enrollment in the tuition-free program.
- The testing department will register you at an approved site closest to your home address.

**7. Graduation Requirements**
- Seniors must complete all required credits and pass five STAAR End-of-Course (EOC) exams: Algebra I, English I, English II, Biology, and U.S. History.
- At least the last year of high school credits (25%) must be earned through Texas Tech K-12.

**8. Next Steps**
- Begin your application as soon as possible to ensure timely processing.
- For questions or assistance, contact Texas Tech K-12 at 1-800-692-6877 or email ttuk12@ttu.edu.

**Helpful Links**
- [Full-time Tuition-Free Diploma Program (TX Residents Only)](https://www.depts.ttu.edu/k12/freetuition/)
- [Full-time Tuition-Paid Diploma Program](https://www.depts.ttu.edu/k12/paid-tuition/)
- [Support Portal](https://support.k12.ttu.edu/k12?id=report_issue&sys_id=043a96811b358e50239f0e1de54bcbeb)

**Summary**
- Apply online, submit required documents, and select your program.
- For tuition-free, participate in the lottery; for tuition-paid, enroll anytime.
- Meet course load, progress, and testing requirements.
- Contact Texas Tech K-12 for support throughout the process.

**Discussion-Based Assessment (DBA) Information for Parents – Texas Tech K-12**

- A Discussion-Based Assessment (DBA) is a required oral assessment in many Texas Tech K-12 courses.
- The DBA is typically conducted by the course teacher and is designed to assess the student’s understanding of key course concepts through a conversation or discussion.
- DBAs are often scheduled at specific points in the course, such as before a major exam or at the end of a unit/module.

**Purpose of the DBA**
- To verify the student’s understanding of the material.
- To provide an opportunity for students to explain their reasoning and thought process.
- To ensure academic integrity in an online learning environment.

**How DBAs Work**
- The student will schedule a time to meet with their teacher, usually via phone or video conference.
- The teacher will ask questions related to the course content.
- The student is expected to respond in their own words, demonstrating their knowledge and understanding.

**For Parents**
- DBAs are an important part of the assessment process and help ensure your child is mastering the material.
- Encourage your student to review their notes and course materials before the DBA.
- Remind your student to communicate with their teacher if they have questions about scheduling or preparing for the DBA.

**Next Steps**
- If you have specific questions about DBAs in your child’s course, please contact the course teacher directly through the Texas Tech K-12 portal or Canvas.
- For general support, you may contact Texas Tech K-12 at 1-800-692-6877 or ttuk12@ttu.edu.
